scheme_name: Incentive For The Devadasi Children’s Marriage to Schedule Tribe
description:
The "Incentive For The Devadasi Children’s Marriage to Scheduled Tribe" scheme is a significant initiative launched by the Government of Karnataka in India. 

This scheme was officially launched in the year 2006. 

It aims to provide financial assistance to the children of Devadasis who marry individuals from Scheduled Tribes. 

The historical context of this scheme is rooted in the social stigma and challenges faced by Devadasi women and their children. 

The Devadasi system is a traditional practice in some parts of India where young girls are dedicated to temple service and often face social ostracism. 

This scheme seeks to empower the children of these women by facilitating their marriage into Scheduled Tribes. 

The primary objective of the scheme is to reduce the social stigma associated with the Devadasi system. 

It also aims to promote the welfare of Devadasi children by ensuring they have a better future through marriage into Scheduled Tribes. 

The scheme has a measurable target of providing financial assistance to at least 1,000 beneficiaries annually. 

The financial assistance provided under this scheme is set at INR 50,000 per marriage. 

This amount is intended to help cover the costs associated with marriage, including ceremonies and related expenses. 

The eligibility criteria for this scheme are specific and detailed. 

The applicant must be a child of a registered Devadasi. 

The age limit for the bride is set at a minimum of 18 years. 

There is no upper age limit specified for the bride. 

The groom must belong to a Scheduled Tribe as recognized by the Government of India. 

The family income of the applicant must not exceed INR 1 lakh per annum. 

This income limit is set to ensure that the benefits reach the economically weaker sections of society. 

To apply for the scheme, the applicant must follow a specific process. 

The first step is to obtain the application form from the local Gram Panchayat office or the Department of Women and Child Development. 

The application form can also be downloaded from the official Karnataka government website. 

The applicant must fill out the form with accurate details regarding their identity and family background. 

Required documents include a caste certificate of the groom, proof of the bride's age, and a certificate confirming the bride's status as a child of a Devadasi. 

Additionally, an income certificate must be submitted to verify the family's financial status. 

Once the application form and documents are ready, they must be submitted to the local Gram Panchayat office. 

The application will then be reviewed by the concerned authorities. 

The disbursement of the financial assistance is typically processed within three months of the application submission. 

The scheme operates on a continuous basis and does not have a specific deadline for applications. 

However, it is advisable to apply well in advance of the marriage date to ensure timely processing. 

The implementing authority for this scheme is the Department of Women and Child Development, Government of Karnataka. 

They are responsible for overseeing the application process and disbursement of funds. 

Contact details for the department can be found on the official Karnataka government website. 

The scheme has seen a positive impact on the lives of many Devadasi children since its inception. 

It has contributed to reducing the stigma associated with the Devadasi system. 

By facilitating marriages into Scheduled Tribes, the scheme promotes social integration. 

As of the latest reports, over 5,000 beneficiaries have received assistance under this scheme since its launch. 

The scheme has also been instrumental in raising awareness about the rights of Devadasi women and their children. 

In addition to financial assistance, the scheme encourages community participation in supporting Devadasi families. 

Awareness programs are conducted to educate the community about the benefits of the scheme. 

These programs aim to change societal perceptions regarding the Devadasi system. 

The government has also collaborated with non-governmental organizations to enhance the reach of the scheme. 

Monitoring and evaluation mechanisms are in place to assess the effectiveness of the scheme. 

Feedback from beneficiaries is collected to improve the implementation process. 

The scheme is part of a broader initiative by the Government of Karnataka to empower marginalized communities. 

It aligns with the state's commitment to social justice and equality. 

The financial assistance provided is a one-time grant aimed at alleviating the financial burden of marriage. 

The scheme not only supports the children of Devadasis but also promotes the dignity of women in society. 

It serves as a model for similar initiatives in other states across India. 

The success of the scheme has prompted discussions on expanding its benefits to include educational support for Devadasi children. 

Overall, the "Incentive For The Devadasi Children’s Marriage to Scheduled Tribe" scheme represents a significant step towards social reform. 

It addresses the historical injustices faced by Devadasi women and their families. 

By providing financial support for marriage, the scheme helps to ensure a more secure future for Devadasi children. 

The initiative reflects the government's commitment to uplift marginalized communities and promote social welfare. 

In conclusion, this scheme is a vital part of the efforts to eradicate the Devadasi system and support the rights of women and children in India. 

It stands as a testament to the importance of targeted welfare schemes in addressing specific social issues. 

The ongoing success of the scheme will depend on continued government support and community involvement. 

The future of the scheme looks promising as it continues to evolve and adapt to the needs of its beneficiaries. 

This initiative is a crucial part of the broader narrative of social justice in India. 

It highlights the importance of addressing historical injustices through targeted welfare programs. 

The scheme not only provides financial assistance but also fosters a sense of dignity and respect for the Devadasi community. 

It is a significant step towards creating a more equitable society for all.
